narrative.overview:
The landing world is borrowed, by the user's choice, from a resort virtual tour (the Avoriaz site recorded in `AVORIAZ_STYLE_GUIDE.md`; that file describes the external source, not this project). The source's grammar maps onto the product: the visitor's own profile sentences fill the screen the way a 360° panorama does, and simulated critiques pin to individual sentences as round apricot hotspots. Text is the imagery. There is no photography, and none is needed.

The material is flat, full-bleed planes of colour stacked as the page scrolls: a deep navy field, a drenched apricot band, a white sheet, then a black close. Type does almost all the expressive work: extra-condensed uppercase Archivo at poster sizes, sometimes outlined, with an apricot fill that wipes in from the left to mark what is being looked at. Motion is slow and deliberate (0.5s to 0.7s) rather than snappy.

**Scope.** This world currently covers the landing page (`/`) only, scoped under the `.pf` root class in `src/app/landing.css`. The `/studio` route deliberately keeps its older "Aero" look (`src/app/globals.css` and the shadcn tokens). That split is known, and whether to migrate the studio is still an open decision. Nothing in this file describes the studio, and the Aero tokens are not the target.
keyCharacteristics: One committed accent (apricot) on navy, black, and white grounds.
Extra-condensed uppercase display (Archivo, `wdth` 62) at poster scale.
Outlined lettering with an apricot clip-path wipe as the "this one" signal.
Square corners or full circles only (plus the pill-shaped platform switch). No shadows.
Navy text on apricot, never white, because white on apricot fails contrast.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Apricot is the only hue. Any second colour is a neutral (navy, slate, ink, black, white, grey).

rules.name: The Navy-on-Apricot Rule
rules.body: Text and icons on an apricot fill are navy. This is a deliberate departure from the source's white-on-apricot, which fails WCAG contrast.

rules.name: The Condensed Caps Rule
rules.body: Anything that names, labels, or commands is set in condensed uppercase (`font-stretch: 62%` plus `font-variation-settings: "wdth" 62`). Anything meant to be read as a paragraph is set at normal width and in sentence case.

rules.name: The Outline-and-Wipe Rule
rules.body: Outlined lettering (transparent fill, white stroke) means "not yet looked at". An apricot copy revealed with a left-to-right `clip-path` wipe means "this one". Use it for the panorama's lit sentence and the closing "you." only, not as decoration.

rules.name: The Flat Plane Rule
rules.body: Separate surfaces with a change of ground colour or a 1px hairline, never a shadow or a blur.

rules.name: The Square or Round Rule
rules.body: A corner is either 0 or fully round. No intermediate radii (4px, 8px, 12px). The 80px switch pill is the only rounded rectangle, and it is reserved for toggles.

dos: **Do** put navy text and icons on every apricot fill.
**Do** keep corners at 0 or 50%; reserve the 80px pill for the platform switch.
**Do** set names, labels, and controls in condensed caps (`wdth` 62), and reading text at normal width.
**Do** use the 0.5s `cubic-bezier(0.65, 0, 0.35, 1)` ease for state changes and the 0.7s `cubic-bezier(0.165, 0.84, 0.44, 1)` ease-out for entrances, and honour `prefers-reduced-motion`.
**Do** cite segment and fact IDs in tabular uppercase wherever a critique or flag points at text.
**Do** draw unlit panorama sentences solid (white at 86%) rather than outlined at 640px and below, where a 1.5px stroke at 22px closes the counters.
donts: **Don't** use box-shadows, blurs, or glows to separate surfaces.
**Don't** use intermediate corner radii or rounded cards.
**Don't** show ratings as percentages, stars, or bare bars without the rating word.
**Don't** apply these tokens to `/studio` until the migration decision is made; it still runs the Aero system.
